Subject: Reforestation + carbon credit project — GBP 1m impact ticket

Good afternoon, There is an opportunity to combine degraded land restoration in Ogun State with a verified carbon credit pipeline that yields environmental and social co‑benefits. The proposal is GBP 1m for land preparation, saplings and three years of maintenance to sequester an estimated 30,000 tCO2 over 20 years. Revenue assumptions are conservatively priced at GBP 6 per tCO2 (current voluntary market base), producing a potential IRR of 8–10% when carbon revenue is included and higher if biodiversity or PES premiums are secured. Impact metrics include hectares restored, tonnes CO2 sequestered and 150 local jobs during planting seasons. From a risk perspective, verification and permanence are central, with dangers from baseline overestimation and land tenure disputes; mitigants include third‑party VCS/Gold Standard validation, buffer credits for permanence and binding community land‑use agreements. Recommendation: allocate GBP 1m with an immediate verification budget and a 120‑day baseline assessment, subject to successful title and community consent. I can introduce the project team and the verifier within ten days. Regards, Marcus

Subject: Pilot solar mini‑grids in Ondo State — GBP 500k phased entry

E kaaro, I hope you are well. Rural communities in Ondo State still face daily power interruptions that constrain small businesses; a compact solar mini‑grid pilot can unlock productivity gains while delivering measurable social returns. The investment ask is GBP 500k capex for a phased pilot covering three villages (approximately 1,200 households and 250 micro‑enterprises). Under conservative demand and tariff assumptions we model an IRR of 12–14% over a 10‑year concession, breakeven in year 4. Impact metrics: 1,200 households electrified, estimated cost per beneficiary GBP 416 (capex amortised over 10 years), and expected incremental revenue uplift for micro‑enterprises of 15–20% within 12 months. From a risk perspective, key exposures are regulatory clarity on mini‑grid tariffs, NGN FX volatility for remittances and meter‑level payment collection; mitigation measures include a fixed‑indexation tariff clause, partial NGN/GBP cashflows layering and a third‑party collections partner with mobile money integration. Recommendation: proceed with a phased pilot (GBP 500k capex), subject to site due diligence and a 90‑day tariff negotiation with the state regulator. If agreeable, I will share the full financial model and propose a site visit within three weeks. Best regards, Marcus Adeyemi

Good afternoon, Rapid urbanisation in Greater Accra has created a persistent shortage of affordable rental housing for middle‑income workers; a blended finance JV can bridge the gap while preserving investor returns. The proposal is an GBP 8m development blending concessional debt (40%), mezzanine impact capital (20%) and equity (40%) to deliver 160 units at average build cost GBP 40k per unit, targeting monthly rents equivalent to 60% of market for five years. Financially, we expect a project IRR of 11–13% for equity under the structure and an implied cost per subsidised unit (concessional subsidy component) of GBP 10k. From a risk perspective, exposures include title clarity, construction cost inflation and tenant affordability; mitigants are third‑party title insurance, fixed‑price EPC contracts with inflation collars and a phased leasing approach with employer‑linked rental guarantees. Recommendation: proceed to term negotiation with a target signature in 90 days, subject to a 60‑day technical and legal due diligence. If this fits your appetite I will circulate the term sheet and the pro forma within five business days. Best, Marcus

Amina sat in front of her computer, eyes fixed on the screen as she watched the numbers tick up: 200 users, 500, 1,000. Her product had finally shipped, and the first users were trickling in. She felt a rush of excitement, but also a hint of trepidation. What if they didn't like it? What if they didn't pay?

task_instruction: Short investment proposition to attract institutional capital into a district-scale solar-plus-storage project.
task_details: Write a formal executive note for the council finance committee summarising the project case for an 8 MW solar PV plus 12 MWh battery storage facility on council-owned land. Provide one-line conclusion, recommended procurement model and financing structure, projected capex/opex, indicative revenue streams and IRR, public subsidy required (if any), expected carbon abatement per year, stakeholders, timeline to financial close, governance and risk mitigations. Include two KPIs and a final recommendation with next steps.
personalized: Conclusion: Proceed to market with a long-term ground lease and availability payment structure to deliver an 8 MW solar PV and 12 MWh battery storage asset that generates stable cashflow and local clean-energy benefits. Recommendation: adopt a long-lease concession with private developer equity and institutional debt (expected capex GBP 6.4m; opex GBP 40k pa). Rationale: limits headline public capex while unlocking private capital and operational expertise (timeline: tender 4 months; financial close 9–12 months). Recommendation: target a base-case equity IRR of 7–9% and structure revenue from merchant power sales, capacity contracts and a small council availability payment capped at GBP 150k pa for 5 years, contingent on delivery. Rationale: delivers bankable returns while sharing market risk; expected annual generation ~9.2 GWh and carbon abatement ~2,000 tCO2e pa. Recommendation: require community benefit package (1% revenue share) and local labour clauses. Rationale: secures social returns and political acceptability. Governance: Energy SPV, council representative on governance board, independent technical advisor, pension fund debt anchor preferred. Key risks: grid connection delay (mitigation: early engagement with DNO), merchant price volatility (mitigation: blended offtake contracts). KPIs: MW installed and % of local labour hours on site. Next steps: instruct detailed procurement documents and shortlist prospective developers; subject to verification of grid capacity, I can lead investor outreach.

In the heart of an industrial park, a behemoth of steel and concrete stretched as far as the eye could see. The air was thick with the smell of fuel and the constant rumble of engines, a stark reminder of the park's energy woes.
